Email Mission The Transportation Technologies Office (TTO) forges strategic partnerships and invests in research, development, and demonstration (RD&D) of technologies to advance U.S. transportation systems. TTO works to lower transportation costs for American families and businesses, improve the affordability of goods, strengthen domestic supply chains, and support U.S. manufacturing in the transportation sector. Priorities Lowering transportation costs can have a significant impact on American households by making it cheaper to get around town and cheaper to buy goods that are transported around the country by truck, rail, and air. Advances in transportation technology can help lower these costs, expand the use of abundant domestic materials, and support national security. TTO collaborates with industry, governments, National Laboratories, universities, and other research institutions to advance transportation technologies and solutions. pages.text: Transportation | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Transportation More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design We all need transportation to travel to job interviews, commute to work, and participate in work-related trainings. Accessible, reliable transportation ensures that Americans with disabilities can actively participate in the labor force and gain meaningful employment. Public transportation systems have increasingly ensured greater accessibility, but many people with disabilities still can't access transportation to work. Access to public transit and for-hire transportation for people with disabilities includes many aspects of accessibility. The diversity of disability means that transportation needs to consider cognitive, sensory, and physical and mobility access. Improving access to transportation requires travel trainings, coordination of resources, and trainings on rights. ODEP has collaborated with the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and other Federal agencies to increase access to transportation to work. For instance, ODEP participates on the Coordinating Council on Access and Mobility managed by DOT. This Federal interagency initiative supports state and local governments as they develop coordinated systems to assist older adults, people with disabilities, and individuals of low income to access transportation to work and participate actively in the community. Tratamiento de la influenza 23 de abr. del 2026 English (US) Vistazo general Si se enferma de influenza, una opción de tratamiento pueden ser los medicamentos antivirales contra la influenza. Los medicamentos antivirales pueden hacer que la enfermedad sea más leve y acortar el periodo en el que está enfermo. También pueden prevenir algunas complicaciones por la influenza, como la neumonía. Los medicamentos antivirales contra la influenza son más eficaces si se inician de forma temprana, idealmente entre los dos días de la aparición de los síntomas de la influenza. Información general sobre el tratamiento Los antivirales contra la influenza son medicamentos recetados (pastillas, solución líquida, polvo para inhalar o solución intravenosa) que combaten la influenza en sus vías respiratorias. Los medicamentos antivirales no se venden sin receta médica. Solo puede conseguirlos en una farmacia si tiene una receta de su médico o proveedor de atención médica. More than 30 years later, the collective, led by Big Tony Fisher, still fills sold-out venues with heavyweight percussion and call-and-response lyrics. TSCA Section 21 Under TSCA section 21, any person may petition EPA to initiate a proceeding for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule or order under: Section 4 -- rules or orders requiring chemical testing; Section 6 -- rules imposing regulatory controls on chemicals; Section 8 -- rules requiring information; or Section 5(e) or (f) -- orders affecting new chemical substances. The petition must be filed in EPA's Office of the Administrator and set forth the facts that are claimed to establish the necessity for the action requested. EPA is required to grant or deny the petition within 90 days from the day the petition is filed with EPA. If EPA grants the petition, EPA must promptly commence an appropriate proceeding. If EPA denies the petition, the reasons for denial must be published in the Federal Register. Обозначение обособленной велосипедной дорожки: highway=cycleway - основной тег линии, который указывает, что путь предназначен для движения на велосипедах. foot=no - явно запрещает движение пешеходов (если пешеходам запрещено находиться на этой дорожке). Если пешеходы разрешены, но дорожка разделена на зоны, используют foot=yes и segregated=yes/no . Велосипедная дорожка + тротуар: Комбинация тэгов для обозначения пешеходного тротуара, совмещённого с выделенной велосипедной дорожкой, которая конструктивно или визуально отделена от пешеходной зоны: highway=footway - обозначает, что данный объект является обустроенной дорожкой, предназначенной в первую очередь для пешеходов. footway=sidewalk - уточняет тип пешеходной дорожки. Этот тег указывает, что дорожка является тротуаром, то есть идет параллельно автомобильной дороге (обычно повторяя её геометрию). bicycle=designated - указывает на официальный юридический статус для велосипедистов. Это значит, что дорожка специально выделена/предназначена для движения на велосипеде (например, установлен соответствующий знак или нанесена разметка), а не просто «разрешена для транзита». segregated=yes - означает, что потоки пешеходов и велосипедистов разделены. We experience it at every moment. And refining our ability to measure it has had immense impact on our world. Surveyors measure local gravity every time they go out in the field. The scientific field of geodesy, which maps the Earth’s shape and predicts where water will flow and minerals can be found, is built on a foundation of gravity measurements. Accurate measurements of gravity are also key to how the world defines the kilogram, the fundamental unit of mass. Today’s most accurate gravity sensors use lasers and atomic clocks to measure how fast a macroscopic reflective object falls in vacuum. But scientists believe that a gravimeter based on the quantum properties of atoms could advance the frontier of precision and accuracy, potentially opening up new and powerful applications. Quantum gravimeters measure gravity’s effect on falling atoms. To do so, they use the fact that quantum-scale objects such as atoms are not just particles but also waves. Close Tuwewanzi's Diary Basic Overview of the Dakota/Lakota Language Posted by Tuwewanzi on 12 November 2026 in English . Dakota (instead called Lakota by speakers of that dialect ) is the indigenous language of the Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ (Seven Council Fires) people of North America, consisting of the Bdewaḳaƞṭuƞwaƞ, Waḣpeḳute, Waḣpeṭuƞwaƞ, Sisiṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞna and Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ communities. Most members of these communities will describe themselves as Dakota (or Lakota for the Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ) people. Dakota and Lakota communities can be found in Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Montana, Manitoba and Saskatchewan. All of these places have a rich geography of names devised by Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ people in the Dakota/Lakota language, including rivers, lakes, towns, islands, hills and more. People have traveled since the dawn of human history and some areas once had Dakota/Lakota communities that presently do not, and so other areas (such as Wisconsin, Iowa, Wyoming and Ontario) also have locations with names in the language. Historically, there have been far, far more Dakota and Lakota place names than those that survive for us to learn about them in the present. Last updated on 17 November 2026. My mapping on OpenStreetMap includes names in both Dakota and Lakota, with ISO codes dak and lkt respectively. This is an unusual approach compared to a lot of other multilingual mapping, so it’s worth explaining in more detail. Dakota and Lakota are two different dialects of the same language (and are two possible names for that language). They are mutually intelligible, and a fluent speaker of one can understand a fluent speaker of the other without difficulty. An analogy might be made to the Spanish spoken in Mexico vs the Spanish spoken in Spain - a speaker of the other dialect will seem to have a strong accent, unusual pronunciation, and some different word choices, but they are still clearly speaking your language . Both dialects are endangered, but there are substantially more Lakota speakers than Dakota speakers and this has been true for a long time. Dakota and Lakota share the vast majority of their vocabulary. Most words that differ between these dialects differ in predictable, formulaic ways that do not represent any difference in meaning (e.g. Oṭuƞwe vs Otȟúŋwahe or Bde vs Ble). The most meaningful differences in Lakota vs Dakota speech emerge in conversational flow, which rarely matters for place names. The Dakota/Lakota language has been a written language for only the most recent chapters of its history. Writing systems for the language were first devised by 19th-century missionaries who sought to promote literacy as a part of encouraging Dakota people to convert to Christianity. These missionaries, especially Stephen Riggs , developed an alphabet based on the Latin Alphabet to represent the sounds present in the language. All widely used methods for writing the language today are based on Riggs’ system with some degree of variation. There is no single writing system accepted by the vast majority of speaker communities. A variety of systems - or orthographies - exist with varying degrees of popularity, and invididual speakers and teachers often have strong preferences one way or another. Areas of debate include: May an orthography make use of special characters (ŋ, ǧ, ḳ, ú) or should writing be done only with characters that can be written with a standard English keyboard? The language contains vowels (a, i, u) that may be nasalized or not, depending on context; should the orthography note the difference? The language contains consonants (z, c, p, t, k, s) that may be aspirated for a harder sound or unaspirated; should the orthography note the difference? pages.text: Two Centuries After This Bronze Leg Emerged From a Scottish Bog, Archaeologists Believe It May Have Belonged to a Towering Statue of a Roman Emperor on Horseback Skip to main content Curator Fraser Hunter examines the bronze leg. Duncan McGlynn In 1820, a larger-than-life gilded bronze lower leg was pulled out of a bog in the Scottish Borders region. For more than two centuries, historians discredited the idea that the Roman-era artifact came from Scotland, instead assuming that it was hacked off a monument in England and hauled north by marauding tribes. But ahead of “ Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire ,” an exhibition at the National Museum of Scotland (NMS), researchers have determined that the so-called “Milsington leg” was not stolen from the south, nor was it violently severed. Instead, they posit that it formed part of a colossal equestrian statue of the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius that once stood in southern Scotland in the second century C.E., before it was dismantled by retreating Roman troops. “This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome’s second attempt at conquering Scotland,” Fraser Hunter , principal curator of prehistoric and Roman archaeology at NMS, says in a statement . The bronze leg shows no signs of being violently hacked off the larger statue. Nếu bạn đủ điều kiện, bạn có thể sử dụng tín thuế này để giảm các khoản thuế bạn nợ – và có thể tăng tiền hoàn thuế của mình. Ai đủ điều kiện Bạn có thể yêu cầu được nhận EITC nếu thu nhập của bạn ở mức thấp đến trung bình. Khoản tín thuế của bạn có thể thay đổi nếu bạn có những đứa trẻ hoặc người phụ thuộc, bạn bị tàn tật hoặc đáp ứng các tiêu chí khác. U.S. Gridded Methane Emissions The gridded EPA U.S. methane greenhouse gas inventory (gridded methane GHGI) includes time series of annual methane emission maps with 0.1° x 0.1° (~ 10 x 10 km) spatial and monthly temporal resolution for the contiguous United States (CONUS). This gridded methane inventory is designed to be consistent with methane emissions from the U.S. EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks (U.S. GHGI). The gridded methane GHGI dataset includes annual methane emission fluxes for over 25 inventory emission source categories, including those from agriculture, petroleum and natural gas systems, coal mining, and waste. Gridded methane emissions data are generated by allocating national annual U.S. GHGI methane emissions from individual source categories to a 0.1° x 0.1° CONUS grid, using a series of spatial and temporal 'proxy' datasets at the state, county, and grid levels. Where possible, proxy data are the same data used to develop the U.S. GHGI so that the gridded emissions can be, as closely as possible, a spatial and temporal representation of the national-level U.S. GHGI. pages.text: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Yolande Knell , Middle East correspondent, Jerusalem and Victoria Bourne AFP via Getty Images A heavy storm earlier this month damaged tents and caused widespread flooding The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire". The foreign ministers warn recent floods have brought "further suffering" to the war-torn territory, which recently had its first winter storm. The statement says 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border. The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory. It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms". The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs said the widespread flooding and a landslide led to a number of deaths, thousands of damaged shelters and the suspension of critical services.
